content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository pulp-platform_riscv-dbg_pr155, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# `sberror` not clearing properly causes OpenOCD interoperability issues
The OpenTitan project uses GDB/OpenOCD to develop top-level debug and manufacturing test cases. We have noticed some test failures when performing unaligned system bus accesses (see [here](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/17729#issuecomment-1488923308)).
In short, when an unaligned read operation is performed, `sberror` is set to 3 (which is correct according to the spec), but after, OpenOCD tries to clear the error with a W1C, by sending 0x7, however, the `sberror` field fails to clear. We believe there is an RTL bug described [here](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/17729#issuecomment-1489076212).
Could someone confirm / fix?

I focused on where the SBERROR register is defined, updated, and accessed over DMI/W1C to clear the error:

- The SBA block itself (`dbg_sba.sv`) is ultimately responsible for capturing and clearing the error; if it never sees the “write-1” clear or is holding the error flag in a state machine, it needs fixing first.
- The register‐file wrapper (`dbg_regfile.sv`) is where register write semantics (especially W1C fields) are implemented; it must decode a W1C to actually clear SBERROR.
- The DMI interface (`dbg_dmi.sv`) is what translates an external bus write into the regfile write; it must correctly route a write-1 to SBERROR.
- Finally, the register definitions (`dbg_regs.svh`) must tag SBERROR as a W1C field so that the above logic can treat it properly.

``` 
src/rtl/dbg_sba.sv
src/rtl/dbg_regfile.sv
src/rtl/dbg_dmi.sv
src/rtl/dbg_regs.svh
```
